I will think this through the way I always do — start from what I did last year, and see what needs changing.

I have 15 mu. Like the past many years, I split it up. Cotton brings in cash, so I keep 5 mu for cotton on the drier corner. The other 10 mu I do wheat in winter and maize in summer — everyone around here does it this way, the land stays busy.

**Wheat (10 mu, planted October):**
Before sowing I spread compound fertilizer — I buy 15-15-15, about 1.5 bags (75 jin) per mu. That is how my neighbor does it and his wheat looks fine. Then after winter, at returning-green, I topdress urea, about half a bag (20 jin) per mu. I have the well, so I water 4 times — before winter freeze, greening, jointing, and filling. Spray herbicide in spring, then 2 more sprays for aphids and yellow rust. Usually I harvest around 900 jin per mu. I use improved seed, same variety as last year — it did not get sick.

**Maize (10 mu, after wheat in June):**
No-till straight after wheat, everyone does this now. One bag of compound with the seeder, then at big-trumpet stage I topdress 1 bag urea per mu. Water once or twice if June is dry. Spray once for corn borer. Hybrid seed of course, the dealer sells a variety most people here use. Expect about 1100 jin per mu.

**Cotton (5 mu):**
Cotton is tiring and costs more, but the price is good and my family helps with picking. I plough before April planting. Put 1.5 bags compound as base, then half a bag urea at flowering. Water 2-3 times. Cotton gets sprayed many times — I count 6 or 7 for bollworm and aphids. Use the Bt-type improved seed, neighbor said bollworm damage is less. Maybe 450 jin seed cotton per mu.

My husband and son work outside so money for fertilizer is not too tight, but I still do not waste. I would rather put on enough than see thin wheat and regret it later.
